idiom_name: overloaded methods on marker structs, or C# 11 static abstract interface members for generic code
implementation_notes: C# resolves overloads at compile time, so passing a per-tag marker struct to a set of overloaded methods realizes the literal pattern for a closed set known at the call site - the tag is never read, and the JIT removes it for value types. The generic form has no equivalent: a type parameter is not usable to rank overloads because generics are a runtime construct whose implementation is shared across reference-type arguments (only value types are monomorphized, by the JIT), so per-type behaviour must come from a type parameter constrained by an interface that declares the per-type members - C# 11 static abstract members, the mechanism behind generic math. What replaces the classic structure: for closed sets, overloads on tag types; for generic algorithms, static abstract interface members called on the type parameter (T.Zero, T.Parse(...)). The classic form is still justified when the set of types is closed, when the tag comes from a value the caller holds, or when the type cannot be constrained by an interface.
pitfalls: Static abstract members can only be invoked on a type parameter (T.M), never through the interface itself, so the 'tag' must travel as a type parameter - an interface with static abstracts cannot even be used as a type argument unless every member has a most specific implementation.

For reference-type arguments the JIT shares one code body, so there is no guaranteed per-type specialization: what looks like compile-time dispatch is a constrained virtual call that may be devirtualized and inlined, which the runtime does not promise - the optimization happens at run time and 'the best you can do is hope'.
Bypassing the tags by taking object, dynamic or params object[] turns the call into runtime type tests; the compile-time selection disappears without any compiler complaint.

Operators force CRTP-shaped constraints (where T : IAdditionOperators<T, T, T>), so the tag/self type must be threaded through every generic abstraction, which is heavier than the C++ trait it imitates.
